title: Resilience-first sales narrative (experiment) - WIP
content:
Goal: prototype a short deck + battlecard set that positions Redwood as the ‘resilience-first’ inference partner for regulated, latency-sensitive apps.

Context / why this experiment
- We get a lot of enterprise questions framed as “can you keep us online under load and compliance pressure?” not just "is the model accurate". Need an approachable narrative that stitches SLA, fallback, and economics.
- This doc is intentionally compact: 6 slide skeleton + 1 battlecard. Use for pilot calls with platform teams and compliance stakeholders.

Slide skeleton (6 slides, speaker notes)
1) Title + framing (30s)
   - Title: Resilience-first inference for regulated apps
   - One-liner: predictable latency, graceful fallbacks, and auditable behaviour for production LLM features
   - Speaker note: start with a 2-sentence user story (e.g., payments portal, 99.9% uptime during peak)

2) Why resilience matters (45s)
   - Bullet: outages cost trust; model regressions cost product adoption
   - Customer example (anonymized): queued requests during holiday spike -> 12min degradation, operator manual rollback
   - Speaker note: tie to SLOs (p99 latency, throughput under commit)

3) How Redwood thinks about resilience (60s)
   - Smart routing: route by latency/cost/region & instant fallback rules
   - Multi-variant model strategy: primary high-accuracy, fallback quantized cheaper variant
   - Caching + prefix reuse to blunt burst cost while preserving latency
   - Speaker note: call out Dedicated pools and Private control plane as levers for regulated customers

4) Demo flow (90s)
   - Live or recorded: 3 steps
     a) baseline trace: 150ms p50, 320ms p95 on hosted for 512 tokens
     b) trigger capacity pressure (simulate degraded GPU pool) -> automatic fallback to quantized variant, p95 jumps to 450ms but remains available
     c) audit view: token-level cost + fallback trace in Console timeline
   - Speaker note: keep demo < 2 min, avoid heavy model outputs, focus on observability and rollback

5) Economics & tradeoffs (45s)
   - Typical delta: fallback variant reduces unit cost 35–55% with small accuracy delta for templated prompts
   - Reserved vs burst: Dedicated reserved keeps p95 predictable; hosted + fallback keeps availability but can cost more in peak
   - Slide callout: suggested qualification question - "Are you comfortable with automated fallbacks or do you need manual approval windows?"

6) Next steps / qualification (30s)
   - Pilot ask: 4-week scoped pilot, 1 integration engineer, 2 alert-run drills, sample prompts (5k tokens/day)
   - Success criteria: p99 under X ms, fallback rate < 12% during spike, no regulatory flags in audit logs

Battlecard (1-page) - Resilience-first quick reference
- Who this helps: platform teams, SREs, security/compliance leads, payments/fintech product owners
- Hook (10s): Keep product features online with predictable latency & auditable fallbacks — even during model/regional disruptions
- Top objections + suggested responses:
   1) "Automated fallbacks will change outputs and break UX"
      - Response: design prompt sets that degrade gracefully; we recommend output contracts (structured JSON) and a fallback quality gate that prevents fallthrough for critical flows. Pilot will include 200 sample prompts to validate.
   2) "We must keep PII on-prem; hosted is a blocker"
      - Response: Redwood Private provides a customer-managed control plane + optional on-prem package; same API surface, same Console observability. We can run an architecture workshop (1.5 hrs).
   3) "Pricing is unpredictable with autoscaling"
      - Response: propose Dedicated reserved baseline + burst policy; Optimize will estimate batching and cache impact for expected prompt distribution. Provide sample cost spreadsheet during pilot (link in artifact).
   4) "Regulators will ask for change logs/audit"
      - Response: Console exports audit trails per-request + KMS integration for keys. We can demo export to S3/secure bucket.

- Demo cues for SEs (short lines to use during office hours)
   - "Watch the Console timeline when I flip the region routing; you’ll see the fallback hit and audit entry appear"
   - "We’ll pin the model version for you so experiments don’t change behaviour mid-pilot"

- Quick decision lens (two questions)
   - Is p95 latency a hard requirement? If yes -> prioritize Dedicated.
   - Do you need customer-controlled keys/audit? If yes -> Private evaluation.

Open items / TODOs
- [ ] Get sample latency numbers from runtime team for 4 recent models (ticket RED-2741). Diego to follow up.
- [ ] Create 2 short sample prompt sets (customer-facing & compliance-safe). Priya owns.
- [ ] Draft cost spreadsheet for typical payment use-case (Jonah) - include reserved vs burst scenarios.
- [ ] Slide deck: produce two variants — "SRE-focussed" and "Compliance-focussed". (deadline: 2025-03-12)
- [ ] Quick play record (1min) for SE enablement: record console demo showing fallback trace.

Notes to self / rough phrasing that may be useful in slides
- "Resilience-first" is intentionally broad — emphasis is on keeping product observable and recoverable, not only raw accuracy.
- Avoid promising absolute numbers. Use ranges and qualifiers ("typical", "observed in pilot").
- Use customer language: uptime, latency, auditability, cost predictability.

Slack / references
- Slack thread: #sales-resilience (link placeholder)
- Confluence draft: confluence:INFERENCE-RESILIENCE-001 (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira epic: RED-2741 (runtime metrics request)

Risks / guardrails
- Do not promise that fallback variants are always semantically equivalent. Provide examples where we should not fallback (legal text generation, high-stakes decision closures).
- Have explicit rollback/kill-switch playbook in pilot SOW.

Immediate next move (for Ava)
- Schedule 30m workshop slot with runtime on Wednesday to pull latency/cost numbers. Add runtime engineers to RED-2741.
- Share this doc with Diego/Priya/Jonah and ask for the two prompt sets by EOD Monday.
